purpose: Correction of a pseudoreplication error in the initial n=9 Welch's t-test analysis. The 9 episodes per ablation arm are NOT 9 independent samples -- 3 of them are repeated evaluations of the identical trained checkpoint per seed. The correct independent unit is the trained checkpoint (one per seed, n=3 per arm).

flawed_initial_analysis_do_not_cite.method: Welch's t-test treating all 9 episodes as independent

corrected_analysis.method: Per-seed means (3 repeated evaluations averaged per seed) + paired t-test across n=3 shared seeds
corrected_analysis.verdict: Neither reaches p<0.05 at n=3. LowPenalty is numerically CLOSER to significance (p=0.054) than HighDiscovery (p=0.10), the OPPOSITE ranking from the flawed n=9 analysis, because LowPenalty's smaller effect is consistent across all 3 seeds while HighDiscovery's larger effect is driven by 2 of 3 seeds (seed 99 shows almost no gain).

coverage_efficiency_cells_per_meter.method: new_cells_discovered / total_distance_m, per episode, cafe grid = 800 cells
coverage_efficiency_cells_per_meter.note: HighDiscovery shows a clear separation here independent of the underpowered significance test above; supporting (not confirming) the hypothesis that HighDiscovery improves movement efficiency/targeting rather than raw displacement.
